purpose: Read-only diagnosis of the observed clean-sparse GNSS regression; no runtime or threshold tuning.
position_metric: Paired-GNSS approximate base_link proxy, not official fused-reference score.
interpretation: The retained single-rover windows at 480 s and 720 s disagree with the simultaneously recorded master antenna. The latter is available only to this offline diagnosis, not selected for runtime input.
At 720 s rover and master imply longitudinal coordinates differing by approximately 16 m; the normal age, status and small rover lateral residual do not identify this as an invalid fix.
Map heading varies less than 0.4 deg over 20 m at these windows, so tight-curve body-tangent error cannot explain the regression.

The paired-GNSS scoring proxy rejects these invalid baselines at the affected windows and measures persistent odometry error after the pair becomes consistent again. It is still an approximate reference.

The fixed-payload guard does not certify robustness to all biased or jittering single-antenna GNSS. A narrower gate chosen from this validation failure would be tuning rather than independent verification.
runtime_available_channel: RF only in each injected sparse window; paired MF used solely for offline diagnosis.
